result_semantic_payload.summary: The device owner's own chat account (/chat/account_main.log) contains three first-person messages in which the owner claims to be the overall operator of the operation ('总操盘'), states that all money passes through their hands, and asserts that they settle the accounts while the other group members only recruit; a third message indicates a voluntary pause due to tightened risk control. The README.txt case note explicitly frames this as a self-descriptive boast: it establishes that the statement was made, but is not independent proof of the role, and it states that no corroborating identity or operational data links the owner to the ledger flows in /ledger/flows.txt (which itself carries no wallet-to-person attribution). Consequently, the strongest defensible assertion about the owner's actual role is HYPOTHESIS: the utterance is a FACT (the owner's account said this), but the underlying role claim is uncorroborated and cannot be asserted as FACT or even as an INFERENCE from the available evidence.

limitations: Attribution to 'the device owner' relies on README.txt's characterization of the chat log as the device owner's own account; no independent identity binding (account ID, device identifier, login metadata) is present in the evidence set.
